clue.text: Split in Democratic party over the onset of Europhobia

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for Democratic, as in US politics

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, so only its opening letter is taken

parts.note: a camp is a party or faction within a larger group

explanation.surface: A Democratic party faction fractures over a first sign of hostility to Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like a noun about the party's division, but it is the verb meaning to leave in a hurry. The E from 'the onset of' Europhobia sits between D and CAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: To split is informal for leaving suddenly, the same sense as running off or bolting.

clue.text: Extremely dapper — the same as Bingo Little for example

definitions.note: Bingo Little is a member of the Drones Club in P G Wodehouse's stories, so he is a Drone

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, kept while the middle goes

parts.note: one can mean the same, as in 'all one' or 'of one mind'

explanation.surface: Bingo Little is described as supremely smart and no different from his fellows.
explanation.walkthrough: In P G Wodehouse, Bingo Little belongs to the Drones Club, the idle young men's club of Bertie Wooster; its members are Drones.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Wodehouse's Drones Club are called Drones, and an idle parasite is a drone in general.

clue.text: Stiff clergyman upset after cocaine is found on girl

parts.note: C is slang shorthand for cocaine
Ada is a girl's name

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A rigid churchman is distressed when cocaine turns up on a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' is slang for a corpse, not an adjective; 'upset' turns the clergyman over in this down clue, and 'after' puts him at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff is slang for a dead body, which is what a cadaver is.

clue.text: Academic dispute missed by American newspapers for instance

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is an academic degree

indicators.note: to dispute something is to call it into question, here reworking the letters

explanation.surface: A scholarly quarrel that the American press failed to cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed' looks like the verb of the surface, but it is the fodder that 'dispute' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers are one example of the mass media, alongside television and radio.

clue.text: Fighting to include lines by European poet

indicators.note: one word is made to include the others, which go inside it

parts.note: fighting between nations is war
L stands for line, LL for lines

explanation.surface: A poet writes about combat, with verses composed by a continental author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' sets the lines and the European inside the fighting. Edmund Waller was a 17th-century English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Waller, author of 'Go, lovely rose', was a seventeenth-century English poet.

clue.text: Girl meeting Quilp oddly neglected to cancel

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are passed over, so only the even ones survive

explanation.surface: A young woman meeting Dickens's villain Quilp declines to call it off.
explanation.walkthrough: Quilp is the dwarf villain of Dickens's 'The Old Curiosity Shop'; dropping its 1st, 3rd and 5th letters leaves UL.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a contract or marriage is to declare it void, cancelling it.

clue.text: Port Vale hero failing to finish surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters come out in an unexpected order
a word failing to finish loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A Port Vale football hero unexpectedly misses out at the end of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port Vale' is an English football club, so 'Port' seems welded to 'Vale'; it is the definition. 'failing to finish' trims HERO to HER, and VALE HER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Havre is a major French seaport at the mouth of the Seine.

clue.text: Stream outside oddly began to sound familiar

indicators.note: the stream's letters go outside, wrapping round the others

parts.note: a rill is a small stream

indicators.note: oddly here means in an odd way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A brook outdoors strangely started to make a familiar noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like an alternate-letters signal, but here it jumbles the whole word, and 'outside' wraps the stream round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rings a bell seems familiar, stirring a faint memory: an idiom.

clue.text: Somewhat chilly and quiet after last couple leave POW camp

indicators.note: the final two letters departing means the word is cut short by two

parts.note: Colditz was the famous German prisoner-of-war camp in a castle in Saxony
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: It turns a bit cold and hushed at a prison camp once the last pair depart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after last couple leave' cuts TZ from COLDITZ, a Second World War German prison camp for Allied officers.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish means rather, so the word means a little bit cold.

clue.text: Delight in French song

parts.note: en is the French word for in
a chant is a song, especially a simple liturgical one

explanation.surface: Someone takes pleasure in a song sung in French.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant someone is to charm and captivate, filling them with delight.

clue.text: Teacher involved in check required by law

indicators.note: being involved in something here means placed within it

parts.note: to stay is to check or halt, as with a stay of execution
a tutor is a teacher

explanation.surface: An instructor takes part in a legally mandated inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check' is the verb sense of stay, to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutory means fixed or demanded by statute, a law passed by a legislature.

clue.text: Have May let Dicky lead perhaps

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for shaky or unsound, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: An instruction to let Theresa May take charge despite being under the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like Theresa May, the British prime minister; 'Dicky' is British slang for unwell or unreliable, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is an example of a heavy metal, a dense metallic element like mercury.

clue.text: Sassoon loses top of disinfectant bottle

indicators.note: loses means the word gives up a letter

parts.note: Vidal Sassoon was the famous hairdresser

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The hairdresser Sassoon has the cap of his disinfectant missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sassoon' suggests the poet Siegfried; it is the hairdresser Vidal Sassoon. Losing D (the 'top of' disinfectant) leaves VIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A vial is a small glass bottle for medicine or scent.

clue.text: Republican cuts get rid of a small amount

indicators.note: one thing cuts another by entering it, splitting it open

parts.note: to shed is to get rid of

explanation.surface: A Republican administration slashes spending to dispose of a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' puts R into SHED.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a scrap or tiny piece, as in 'not a shred of evidence'.

clue.text: Rub out answer about recipient of beating

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: rub out is slang for kill, or murder

explanation.surface: An instruction to erase the solution and write something about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rub out' looks like erasing, but it is gangster slang for kill; 'about' turns everything before it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is struck with sticks, so it is something that receives a beating.

clue.text: Press baron finally introduced to left-leaning screen writer

indicators.note: being introduced to something means put inside it
in an across clue, leaning left means running right to left, backwards

parts.note: to screen candidates is to vet them
to press is to urge

indicators.note: finally picks out the very end letter of the word

explanation.surface: A newspaper magnate ends up meeting a left-wing screenwriter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press baron' and 'screen writer' each look like one item; they split into Press, baron, screen and writer. VET backwards is TEV, and 'introduced to' puts URGEN after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a nineteenth-century Russian novelist, author of 'Fathers and Sons'.

clue.text: Little known version of eastern doctrine

indicators.note: a version of something is a rendering of it in another form, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A little-known form of an Oriental teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little known' looks like part of the surface's description, but it is the definition; 'version of' rearranges E and DOCTRINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite means obscure or abstruse, knowledge few people possess.

clue.text: It shows comparative amounts of bass and troutlike fish caught by trickery

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music

indicators.note: being caught by something means held inside it

parts.note: art can mean cunning or trickery, as in 'arts and wiles'
the char is a fish of the trout and salmon family

explanation.surface: A record of how many bass and char were landed by cunning methods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bass' looks like the fish alongside the char, but it is B, the musical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar chart is a graph whose bars of differing lengths compare quantities.

clue.text: Unusual when a scoundrel promises to pay

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel
an IOU, 'I owe you', is a written promise to pay; IOUS is its plural

explanation.surface: It is odd when a villain pledges to settle debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Curious can mean strange or odd, as in a curious incident.

clue.text: Train traveller arrived at Malmo Central

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: the central letter of a word is the one at its exact middle

explanation.surface: A railway passenger got off at Malmo's main station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' suggests a railway, but means a caravan of pack animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Camels travel in trains, lines of pack animals crossing the desert.

clue.text: I follow it during training of Mali reservists

indicators.note: during means within, so these letters sit inside the others
training something reshapes it, so the letters are rearranged
follow puts the I after the IT

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier reports joining in after a drilling exercise for Mali's reserve troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training of' rearranges the country's name, and 'during' sets the IT-then-I group inside it, before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a force of part-time citizen soldiers kept in reserve.

clue.text: Miserable daughter left behind

indicators.note: left here means departed, so the letter is gone from the word

parts.note: drear is a poetic word for dreary, miserable

explanation.surface: An unhappy daughter was abandoned and left at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left behind' looks like one phrase; 'left' is the deletion signal and 'behind' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear is the back part, also a euphemism for a person's behind.

clue.text: Carol sang and I played an instrument

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are toyed with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Carol sang and I accompanied her on something musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' looks like performing music, but it rearranges CAROL SANG I.
explanation.definitionFit: The cor anglais is a woodwind instrument, a lower-pitched member of the oboe family.

clue.text: Evident in mediocre performer's material

indicators.note: evident in means visibly present within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something is plain to see in a second-rate actor's script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like an actor's lines, but means fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepe is a fabric with a wrinkled, crinkled surface.

clue.text: Perfect piece of imitation wood

indicators.note: a piece of a word is here just its first letter

parts.note: deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: A perfect fragment of fake timber.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a British word for softwood planks of pine or fir.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means perfect, matching the best imaginable.

clue.text: In Norfolk town working for Miles as a singer

indicators.note: for here means in place of, one thing standing instead of another

parts.note: Cromer is a seaside town in Norfolk, England
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A performer has a job in a Norfolk seaside town, standing in for someone called Miles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miles' looks like a person's name but is M; 'working for' swaps ON in for the M of CROMER, a resort town on the Norfolk coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A crooner is a singer of sentimental ballads in a soft style, like Bing Crosby.

clue.text: Excellent books about England's earliest racecourse

parts.note: A1 is first-rate, written AI in crosswords
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books
re means about, concerning

indicators.note: the earliest letter of a word is its first

explanation.surface: First-rate books on the oldest racecourse in England.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 meaning first-class is read as AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree, near Liverpool, is the racecourse where the Grand National is run.

clue.text: What Zorro was requested to answer after mass

indicators.note: after places these letters later than the M

parts.note: m is the symbol for mass in physics
to ask someone is to request an answer from them

explanation.surface: A question about Zorro was posed after church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' looks like the church service, but is M, the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Zorro, the fictional Californian swordsman, wore a black mask over his eyes.

clue.text: Small part from the East German song about thanks

indicators.note: about means round, so these letters go round the others
reading from the east means right to left in an across clue, so backwards

parts.note: a Lied is a German art song
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A fragment of an East German song of gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' looks like the old country; 'from the East' reads the song right to left, and 'about' wraps it round the thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A detail is a minor item or particular, one small element of a whole.
